title: EIP-8496: Code Reads in Block-Level Access Lists
description: Record in the block access list the code hash of every pre-block bytecode that a block loads
author: Lukasz Rozmej (@LukaszRozmej)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP adds a `code_hash` field to the `AccountChanges` entry of the [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) block access list (BAL). For every account whose pre-block bytecode is executed, copied, sized or checked for a delegation indicator during the block, the field holds the Keccak-256 hash of that bytecode. For every other account the field is empty. The BAL then names every piece of pre-block state that a block reads. When [EIP-7709](./eip-7709.md) is also active, a stateless or proving input for the block can be assembled from the block, its BAL and a state snapshot, without executing the block. ## Motivation [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) records every account and storage slot a block touches. A stateless verifier or a zkVM prover can use the BAL as the index of the pre-state it has to load: the account leaves of every listed address and the storage leaves of every listed key. Bytecode is the one state exception. The BAL records bytecode only when it changes, in `code_changes`. An address that is only called, or whose code is only copied or sized, appears with empty change lists, indistinguishable from an address whose balance was read. Which bytecode a block needs can today only be learned by executing the block, or by over-approximating and shipping the code of every listed address. A witness is therefore still gathered the way it was before BALs existed: execute the block, record what it reads, then prove. This EIP removes the last state read that the BAL does not name. [EIP-7709](./eip-7709.md) removes the only non-state read, by serving `BLOCKHASH` from the storage of the [EIP-2935](./eip-2935.md) history contract so that it appears in `storage_reads`. With both, the block, its BAL and a state snapshot are a complete proving input. A prover assembles the witness by lookup alone, with no execution ahead of proving, and can start collecting it as soon as the BAL arrives, which under [EIP-8146](./eip-8146.md) is before the transactions. Clients already diverge on this point. A witness generator that answers `EXTCODESIZE` from a code size cached by code hash never loads the bytes and omits the code from its witness, while a guest built on the reference implementation reads the code and fails without it. A normative definition of "code read" in the BAL removes that class of interoperability bug and gives witness formats such as [EIP-8025](./eip-8025.md) a complete and checkable definition of their code list. Recording the code hash lets consumers without state, such as witness services or peers exchanging BALs, resolve the bytecode from a hash-keyed code store, deduplicates shared code across accounts, and matches the hash form that [EIP-8298](./eip-8298.md) uses for adopted code. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). ### Definitions - **Pre-block code** of an account is its bytecode at the start of block execution, before the pre-execution system contract calls at `block_access_index = 0`. For an [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) delegated account it is the delegation indicator, not the delegate's code. ### Data Structure `AccountChanges` gains a seventh element, `code_hash`: ```python CodeHash = bytes # 32-byte Keccak-256 hash of bytecode, or empty # AccountChanges: [address, storage_changes, storage_reads, balance_changes, nonce_changes, code_changes, code_hash] AccountChanges = [ Address, # address List[SlotChanges], # storage_changes List[StorageKey], # storage_reads List[BalanceChange], # balance_changes List[NonceChange], # nonce_changes List[CodeChange], # code_changes CodeHash # code_hash (hash of the pre-block code if it was loaded, else empty) ] ``` `code_hash` MUST be RLP-encoded as a 32-byte string when set and as the empty byte string (`0x80`) when not set. All other encoding rules of [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) are unchanged. ### Code Loads A **code load** of address `A` is any of the following events, and only these: 1. A message frame is dispatched with `A` as its code address. This includes the recipient of a transaction with a non-empty `to`, the code address of `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL` and `STATICCALL` after [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) delegation resolution, the targets of pre- and post-execution system contract calls, and the resolved target of every [EIP-8141](./eip-8141.md) frame. The frame counts even if it reverts, halts exceptionally, or is not started because the call fails a post-state gas charge, its sender-balance check or its call-stack-depth check. A call or transaction to a delegated account loads the account under this rule to resolve the delegation, and loads the delegate under this rule when [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) includes it. 2. `EXTCODESIZE` or `EXTCODECOPY` executes with `A` as its target. 3. An [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) authorization names `A` as its authority and the authority account is loaded, whether or not the authorization then succeeds. 4. Transaction validation checks the code of sender `A` under the [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) transaction-origination rule. This loads only the sender's own code, not its delegate's code. 5. When [EIP-8298](./eip-8298.md) is active, `SETCODEFROM` targets source `A` and passes its `SETCODEFROM_SOURCE_GAS` check. This loads only the source's own code, without resolving delegation, whether or not the source is valid, the instruction subsequently runs out of gas, or the enclosing execution reverts. An event is a code load only when [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) records the corresponding address access. In particular an operation that fails its pre-state gas validation of [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md), which includes the [EIP-2929](./eip-2929.md) access costs, loads no code, and `code_hash` can never be set on an address that is absent
